page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7nex.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB memory-per-core ratio. It operates on the x86_64 architecture and includes 48 MB of L3 cache. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and network connectivity is provisioned at a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores, fall within the average range. However, multi-core performance is weaker, placing in the bottom 25% for stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth, both cached and uncached, also ranks in the bottom 25%, though Passmark memory scores and static web serving throughput maintain average tier performance.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.c7nex.xlarge lies in its dedicated CPU allocation versus its constrained memory bandwidth and weak multi-threaded scaling, as evidenced by a poor rating in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and lack of local storage, this instance is suited for workloads that require dedicated CPU cycles but have low memory footprints, such as lightweight web serving, single-threaded processing tasks, and basic utility services.
